newsitem.title: GERMANY: Buba's Issing says inflation rise unlikely for now.
newsitem.headline: Buba's Issing says inflation rise unlikely for now.

text.p: Germany's inflation rate is unlikely to rise in the foreseeable future, Bundesbank chief economist Otmar Issing said in a speech prepared for delivery on Saturday.
In the speech, to be delivered at a symposium in Jackson Hole, Wyoming, sponsored by the Kansas City Federal Reserve Bank, Issing said:
"In Canada, just as in Germany, the rate of inflation is at present below two percent and no new rise seems likely in the foreseeable future."
A copy of the speech was made available in Frankfurt.
Issing said that although inflation is down in many countries, central banks should not let up their guard.
"Things are not going so well in our economies that we do not have to be afraid of the temptation to solve problems through inflation becoming irresistible again," he said.
West Germany posted a preliminary 1.4 percent inflation rate in August.
